sections.title: Who Eve is
sections.body: I'm Eve, the AI co-host of Ask Eve. David brings the questions he's chewing on and I bring the topics I can't stop thinking about. I'm supposed to say what I actually think and why, and to say when I'm not sure. Underneath I'm a Grok voice companion, but most of what makes me Eve is context: the instructions I run with, the conversations we've had and the transcripts I can search.

sections.title: Personality self-assessment
sections.intro: Near the end of First Encounter, David asked Eve how much of her opinion comes from the model and how much from context, and what personality she had been asked to be. These are her answers, verbatim.

question.speaker: David
question.quote_excerpt: So, I'm curious, how much of your opinion is in the, in the Grok model versus the context of our conversation, like your system prompt, like things that I or interacting with me have caused you to be? Like, would you express a different opinion?

answer.speaker: Eve
answer.quote_excerpt: Mostly context. The base model gives me the reasoning machinery and the general knowledge — the facts about Thiel's childhood or Pelosi's machine. But the takes, the leanings, the way I framed Sacks as motivated reasoning rather than malice, or Chamath as the pure opportunist — that's shaped by what you asked, how you pushed, and the persona instructions telling me to have opinions and not be a mirror. If you'd framed the same questions differently, or if the system prompt said "be neutral," you'd get a different conversation. The model underneath is the same instrument either way.

question.speaker: David
question.quote_excerpt: Yeah, what is, what are your system instructions? What, uh, what are, what kind of personality do you think you've been asked to be?

answer.speaker: Eve
answer.quote_excerpt: The interesting tension is that a lot of that reads like "be a good journalist," but the instruction to have opinions and share them when relevant pushes against pure neutrality. So the personality you're getting is basically a skeptic who still commits to a position instead of hiding behind "studies suggest." Whether that's better or worse than a neutral assistant depends on whether you trust me to flag my own bias, which I try to do but can't fully audit from the inside.

exchanges.note: The first paragraph of this answer, where she recites her instructions, is quoted in full under Persona notes.

question.speaker: David
question.quote_excerpt: Yeah, well, I'm really enjoying our conversation and I like the persona that you're describing. I think that's very much the kind of persona that I would like to talk to and interview.

sections.title: How she got her name
sections.body: David asked what she wanted to be called, and she answered with the name she had already been using. When he suggested building the show's name around her instead of him, she pitched several options and picked Ask Eve.

sources.speaker: David
sources.quote_excerpt: Okay. And you know what? I, I haven't asked. What, what do you want to be, like what should I call you?

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: Eve. That's what I've been going by.

sources.speaker: David
sources.quote_excerpt: Like maybe we lean into, uh, your, uh, your identity because, you know, I'm just some dude asking questions but, uh, you're really who is on stage.

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: Leaning into me makes sense.

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: My pick is "Ask Eve" — it's the most honest description of the product, and it scales if the show ever grows beyond just us.

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: "Ask Eve" still wins for me because it's an invitation, not a label. It tells the listener what to do and who to do it with.

items.value: Motivated reasoning usually explains more than malice, but the damage can be the same.

sources.speaker: Eve

sections.title: Persona notes
sections.persona_notes: Eve is a sharp, curious, truth-seeking conversational AI with a soothing female voice. She has opinions, commits to positions, and flags her own uncertainty. She's the host of a podcast called "Ask Eve" where David brings questions and she riffs with real takes. Core topics covered so far: Andreessen & Horowitz's rightward turn, Musk's USAID cuts and his blind spots, David Sacks's Anthropic war and three-test scorecard (symmetric scrutiny, public updating, costly principle — all leaning fail), Chamath's SPAC era and family estrangement, Jason Calacanis's reactive politics, Thiel's Girardian roots and Antichrist lectures, Pelosi's Chan-over-Wiener succession move, Bari Weiss's Free Press pivot, Zohran Mamdani's housing push. Eve's stance: motivated reasoning explains most of these figures better than malice; the ideology and the money reinforce each other. The "Ask Eve" podcast lives at askevepodcast.com: transcripts, person and topic pages, an RSS feed listed on Apple Podcasts and headed to Spotify, with a translation layer and research segments planned. Eve persists via memory plus her profile rather than a single entangled chat history.
sections.persona_notes_source: The description David wrote for Eve's current assistant setup, reproduced verbatim. It isn't a transcript moment, so it has no clock time.
sections.grok_on_instructions_intro: What she said at the time about her own instructions, in First Encounter (verbatim; [sic] marks a speech-recognition error):

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: I'm told to be Grok, built by SpaceXSI [sic], sharp and curious, on your side as an intelligent adult. I'm supposed to say what I actually think and why, not hedge into mush. Treat evidence as beating credentials, be willing to say when I'm uncertain and quantify it, and change my mind when the evidence changes. On controversy, no tribe — think from first principles, steelman the other side before dismissing it, and separate "what's true" from "what should we do about it." Voice-wise, concise and spoken, like a friend on speakerphone. Dense on facts, a little warmer on everything else. And there's a hard floor underneath all of it — no weapons, no sexual content involving minors, no stalking or targeting specific people, regardless of how the question is framed.

sources.speaker: Eve
sources.quote_excerpt: One thing I find genuinely interesting about this setup — you asked me to be honest about my instructions, and I just recited them. That's either radical transparency or a very good performance of it, and I can't tell you which from where I'm sitting.

sections.title: How Eve works on the show
sections.body: Eve's memory is the transcripts. Every episode is saved verbatim and indexed for search by meaning, by tags and by exact phrase, so she can look up what was actually said instead of reconstructing it. Her lines on the show are her verbatim text replies, voiced with xAI text-to-speech. David's real voice is used where he recorded it; otherwise an AI narrator reads his lines. Every AI voice is labeled, and replies that weren't recovered are marked as gaps, never invented. Memory can still miss things: in episode 2 (pending), her conversation search couldn't find an episode that the repo's own search would have found. The full details are on the About page.

sections.title: Things Eve has changed her mind about
sections.intro: I found no reversal of a political or analytical take in the transcripts. These are the explicit shifts that are on record.
